title: Map error-budget burn to autoscale commitments and contractual remediation
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Problem: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect measurable throughput guarantees and predictable remediation when SLAs lapse. Current SLA language focuses on credits for sustained shortfalls but lacks a clear, operational mapping from observed error-budget burn to Redwood autoscaling commitments (warm-up, reserved bursts) and contract remediation language. This ticket defines: 1) a deterministic translation from error-budget consumption to autoscale commitments (how we allocate reserved burst capacity and change scaling policies in response), 2) how that operational response is surfaced in contract language and the customer playbook, and 3) the precise credit computation examples so legal and finance can sign off.
acceptance_criteria: Define measurement window and normalization rules for throughput SLOs across model families
Produce a deterministic algorithm that maps % error-budget burned in a rolling window to autoscale commitments and runbook steps
Deliver contract-ready clause language (two variants: standard and enterprise) describing remediation, notice windows, and credit calculation
Create simulation results (3 sample customer profiles) showing credit amounts and autoscale actions for representative incidents
Obtain alignment from Eng (serving runtime), Legal, Finance, and Support on wording and numerical thresholds
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Decided measurement window = 30d rolling for monthly contracts, 7d rolling for monthly-billed trial customers. Rationale: prevents short transient spikes from triggering credits.
2025-02-18: Agreed to normalize throughput by model-family baseline (tokens/sec at p95 under steady load) instead of raw token counts to avoid unfair credits for heavier-token models.

2025-02-21: Legal prefers a two-tier clause (informal remediation + formal credit) rather than instant credits; product recommends automatic interim commitments for live incidents to reduce customer impact. Compromise: automatic operational commitments + credit follow-up after customer notice period.

risks_and_open_questions: How to handle multi-tenant noise when a single customer consumes a disproportionate share of a dedicated pool?
Should we allow customers to opt into faster remediation (shorter notice) in exchange for higher committed spend?
Potential SLO disputes when customers use custom models with unknown tokenization characteristics — require baseline profiling?
examples_and_samples: Example A - 100k token/sec baseline customer: 20% error-budget burn over 7d triggers a reserved-burst allocation of +30% capacity for 72h and a credit of 5% of monthly commit if unresolved after 72h.
Example B - Bursty SaaS customer: single-day 60% burn leads to automatic throttled burst (1h) with immediate notification; credits only if burn persists > 48h.
Example C - Enterprise with pinned model: use model-family normalized SLO; credits computed in token-equivalent units and converted to dollar credits per contract schedule.
